page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-288 is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the x86_64 architecture. It features 288 virtual CPUs mapped to 144 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor operating at 2.3 GHz. The system is equipped with 2232 GB of RAM, providing approximately 7.75 GB of memory per core. The processor includes a 504 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and int8 operations. No local storage or GPUs are included in this configuration, and it does not bundle complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 312050.11 and a PassMark CPU score of 176858.39. Memory bandwidth is highly competitive, reaching 23049.05 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 1063.61 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. The instance excels in database operations, achieving 36869.2 on PassMark database tests and 405.42 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. However, single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance falling into the average category.

While the server demonstrates strong capabilities in prompt processing for large language models, text generation speeds vary, showing weak performance for small models but remaining average for large 70B models. Given the high memory density and exceptional multi-core throughput, this instance is well-suited for memory-intensive workloads, large-scale database operations, high-throughput web serving, and heavy multi-threaded compilation tasks. The lack of local storage requires external block storage integration, which should be factored into the overall architectural cost efficiency.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-288 is a memory-optimized server configured with 288 vCPUs and 2232 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor running at 2.3 GHz, this x86_64 instance features 144 physical cores with hyperthreading, a 504 MB L3 cache, and support for Intel AMX and AVX-512 instructions. It delivers top-tier multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth, alongside high-throughput database and Redis operations. However, single-core performance is average, and text generation for small LLM models is weak. The instance lacks local storage and GPUs. It is highly suited for memory-intensive databases, enterprise applications, and multi-threaded workloads.
